correctness.rationale: Permutation symmetry makes the averaged Gram operator scalar on the simplex representation. A fixed-order Hilbert--Schmidt recurrence computes that scalar exactly, the arithmetic-geometric sum gives the closed form, and tight-frame isotropy gives the with-replacement baseline. Exact Fraction enumeration through n=5 replays the formulas but is not used as the infinite proof.

evidence: Han--Xie define the same RRK epoch product and prove a general spectral-norm contraction bound, but do not compute the regular-simplex permutation-averaged MSE scalar.
Strohmer--Vershynin prove expected exponential convergence for with-replacement randomized Kaczmarz; on this tight frame it gives the exact one-row baseline, not the reshuffled epoch law.
The 2026 simplex dynamics manuscript uses factors C_i(rho)=1/2[I+rho(uz_i^T+z_i u^T)], not Kaczmarz projectors, and its certified full-reshuffling statements are low-length.

originality.rationale: The closest RRK paper gives a general contraction bound for products of Kaczmarz projections but not the exact permutation-averaged regular-simplex MSE channel. The seminal randomized-Kaczmarz paper supplies the with-replacement baseline only. A 2026 regular-simplex reshuffling manuscript uses a different non-projective factor family and explicitly limits its certified full-reshuffling results to low factor counts; its all-length question is not this Kaczmarz projection identity. Statement-level searches did not locate the closed form or its asymptotic comparison.
residual_risks: Older cyclic-projection, projection-method, or finite-frame literature may encode the same regular-simplex product average under different terminology.
The exact-MSE paper by Agaskar--Wang--Lu was not fully inspectable through the checked public route; an unobserved special-frame corollary remains a source-level risk.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact all-dimensional benchmark for a canonical maximally symmetric overdetermined system and quantifies a strong protocol separation at identical row-action cost: fresh reshuffling leaves Theta(1/n) mean-square error per pass whereas independent with-replacement sampling leaves a constant asymptotic fraction. This isolates a concrete mechanism by which row dependence can matter beyond generic rate bounds.
